messages:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT: GPU capacity exhaustion detected in north-america-prod. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale actions but hit pool_limit. Queue length 1.2k, avg latency 3.8s, p95 tokens/sec drop 45%. Model traffic spike traced to model:v9.1 rollout.
jamal_infra: seeing same in metrics — GPU util ~98% across pool, many pods at OOM_SNAPSHOT in logs. autoscaler error: "scale_limit_reached".
sara_oncall: paging and taking lead. initial impact assessment: affecting hosted API, some customers getting 429s and long tails. Is there a graceful fallback we can flip?
lia_prod: v9.1 changed kv-cache layout and increased context memory ~2x for longer prompts. We saw warmup ramp earlier but didn't expect live traffic pattern to include many long-context requests.
jamal_infra: extracts from infra logs: ```
[2026-03-15T12:42:11Z] pod/inference-xyz OOM_SNAPSHOT: kv-cache exceeded reserved memory
[2026-03-15T12:42:13Z] autoscaler: attempt_scale -> desired=40 current=32 limit=32 -> error scale_limit_reached
[2026-03-15T12:42:19Z] queue_length=1250 enqueue_rate=200/s dequeue_rate=60/s
```
noah_sre: routing table shows 65% of requests got sent to the v9.1 canary (sticky header from client A). We still have model:v9.0 warm in other pools but traffic not evenly balanced.
sam_support: multiple enterprise customers reported errors ~12:40-12:44. Logged: "502/timeout" and "rate_limited". Ticket #PROD-3841 created, pinging account reps.
ops_runbook_bot: runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-exhaustion>. Suggested immediate mitigations: 1) scale limit bump if capacity available 2) enable model fallback routing 3) reduce canary weight to 0 4) enable request-throttling at edge.
sara_oncall: action plan now: (A) reduce v9.1 canary weight to 0, (B) enable model fallback to v9.0 for affected tenants, (C) raise autoscale limit for north-america-prod if clouds show spare quota, (D) enable aggressive KV eviction/disable warmstart for v9.1 pods. Jamal, can you do A and D? Lia, coordinate B. Noah, check quota for C.
jamal_infra: doing A,D now. `rtr set-weight model:v9.1 0 --scope=hosted` -> queued. Also run: `kubectl patch sts inference-v9.1 -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"kv.warmstart":"false","kv.eviction":"aggressive"}}}}}'` -> patch applied to canary pods.
jamal_infra: rtr weight change confirmed. Traffic shift in progress. Rebalancer showing 60% reduction to v9.1 within 30s.
noah_sre: cloud quota check: we have spare GPU quota in us-west-2 but not in us-east-1. north-america-prod is spread across both; can bump pool limit by +12 GPUs if we migrate some pods to us-west-2. That will take ~5-8m.
lia_prod: initiating fallback routing for affected customers: `rtr route --selector=enterprise_tier --model=v9.0` -> applied. Lia: will follow up with targeted rollback of canary for non-enterprise later.
sam_support: informing customers now with initial ETA 20-40m. Posting notes in support tickets.
jamal_infra: autoscaler manual bump attempt: `autoscaler set-pool-limit north-america-prod 44` -> failed (provider quota). Opening cloud support ticket. Meanwhile starting a spot-backed burst pool with preemptible GPUs and routing non-enterprise traffic there: `deploy burst-pool -t spot --model=v9.0` -> deployed.
sara_oncall: good. Also enable edge-level per-client burst throttle to protect control plane. `edgectl set throttle default 50rps` -> applied.
ops_runbook_bot: mitigation checklist updated: traffic weight lowered, model fallback enabled, KV warmstart disabled for v9.1, burst pool created, edge throttle applied. Monitor for dequeue_rate catching up.
jamal_infra: metrics update 60s after mitigations: queue_length -> 680, dequeue_rate -> 150/s, avg latency -> 2.1s, GPU util -> 76% on remaining v9.0 pods.
noah_sre: still seeing some pods with high KV memory due to long-lived sessions; eviction kicked in, pod restarts started, but overall pool stabilizing.
sara_oncall: handoff: I'll stay for coordination for next 30m, then hand to @noah_sre for 4-hour watch. Lia will lead rollback plan if any residual errors. Sam, keep customer comms updated.
lia_prod: planned next steps: full canary rollback for v9.1 to 0 -> verify kv-cache memory diff in staging, add mem cap config to v9.1 runtime, add rollout traffic gating per context-length histogram in future.
sam_support: customers updated, most accepting temporary degradation while we stabilize. Escalated enterprise impacted list to PL and AMs.
sara_oncall: incident severity remains P1 while queue >500 or >5% customer errors. Current status: partial mitigation in place, traffic largely on v9.0 and burst pool, autoscale increase pending cloud. Will update again in 10m and perform official handoff to @noah_sre. :white_check_mark:
noah_sre: taking handoff at 13:15Z. Monitoring dashboards, will escalate back to oncall if regress.
incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: handoff recorded, primary=sara_oncall, secondary=noah_sre, status=stabilizing, start_ts=1765432100, last_update_ts=1765432599."
